visualReview.scope: Detailed rebuilt bridge exterior between its bank bearings.
visualReview.notes: Inspected all ten current portable frames: preview, four sides, arch stones, walkway, cornices, intrados and distant crossing. The recessed mortar core closes the former see-through arch joints. The humpback deck, individually jointed arch and ashlar faces, two cornices, parapets, metal guards and traction strips are complete. Subpixel joints and rails alias in the portable turntable; the shared antialiased close views resolve them.

sharedSurfaceReview.notes: Inspected all ten current shared frames. Metric continuous stone grain supports the physical stone joints without a second conflicting masonry pattern. Arch underside is closed behind recessed joints. Painted iron and rough bank-bearing masonry remain distinct. Actual viewer placement, one read per shared material and model geometry unload pass.

geographicReview.notes: Mapped pedestrian way33924615 fixes the main straight crossing at [17.8150293,43.3372672], heading−0.004339929494839471. North-up rendering agrees with that main span; bent streets in the coarse perimeter continue beyond the separately scoped bearings. LocalY0 is published historical low-water40.05m ASL, giving the documented deck crown60.39m ASL. River stage and host terrain can vary; the asset is not draped to the riverbed.

fidelityReview.notes: 56,312-triangle detailed exterior reconstructed from the restoration technical account:28.71m north span,12.06m rise,3.95m width,0.77m ring and111 radial courses with2–5 stones across. The multi-center arch profile, individual ashlar faces, shaped cornices,0.945m parapets, iron railing, paving and transverse traction strips were compared with primary restoration drawings. Individual stone ordinates, bearing surfaces and minor rail spacing are reconstructed. Adjacent towers, rocky banks, approach streets and internal historical joints are outside this bridge asset.
